title: You did not throw
hook: at Badr, you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw (8:17)
tomorrow: Between a man and his heart

segments.voice: Yesterday: wajilat, hearts that tremble. Your line was a heart that trembles. Today, still at Badr, a verse about who gets the credit.

An award show. The winner reaches the microphone and starts thanking people: my coach, my mom, the team, the crew. Some of it is politeness. But often there's something true in it: the trophy has their name on it, and it was never only them. At Badr, the sources say, the Muslims were badly outnumbered. Commentators report that as the battle began, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ picked up a handful of pebbles and dust and threw it toward the other army. Afterward, a verse came about that throw.
screen: `THE ACCEPTANCE SPEECH.` → `OUTNUMBERED AT BADR.` → `A HANDFUL OF PEBBLES.`

segments.voice: Verse seventeen begins with the believers: you did not slay them, but Allah slew them. Then it turns to the Prophet, in Pickthall's words: “thou (Muhammad) threwest not when thou didst throw, but Allah threw.” In Arabic it's almost a riddle: wa ma ramayta idh ramayta, wa lakinna Allaha rama. You did not throw, when you threw. The verse doesn't deny that the Prophet's arm moved. It says you threw, and in the same breath, it wasn't you. In the verse's telling, both are true at once: the hand was his; the reaching of that handful, and what came of it, was Allah's. The verse goes on: that He might test the believers with a good test from Him. Even victory is a test. Will you say, look at us? The surah opened with an argument over the spoils, and this verse quietly answers it: if the win wasn't only yours, the spoils aren't only yours either. Muslim theologians have long argued over how a human act can be both truly yours and truly from God; different schools gave different answers, and the debate is still taught. The everyday lesson teachers draw is simpler. Effort is real, and it matters. Success is a gift, and it humbles. After good news, a job, a grade, a recovery, Muslims say alhamdulillah, praise be to God. In a way, it's this verse in one word.
screen: `WA MA RAMAYTA — YOU DID NOT THROW.` · `THE HAND WAS HIS; THE REST, ALLAH'S.` · `EVEN VICTORY IS A TEST.` · `EFFORT REAL, SUCCESS A GIFT.` · then, large: `BUT ALLAH THREW.`

segments.voice: Think of one thing you're proud of from this week or this year, and let yourself feel the effort you put in, because it was real. Then widen the picture: the health that let you do it, the people who taught you, the timing you didn't control, the breath in your lungs. If you pray, say alhamdulillah for it; if not, simply credit what wasn't you.
Rama, threw. Surah eight, verse seventeen: you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw. The hand was the Prophet's; the outcome was Allah's. Today's word.
Your line: it wasn't only me. The effort was real, and so was the gift. That's day four hundred seventeen.

original.note: Arabic: and you did not throw when you threw (8:17).

trapdoor: what you thought: God helped win a battle.
what it means: human effort is real, and the outcome belongs to Allah; even a victory is a test.
what a scholar hears: 8:17 is a classic proof-text in debates on human acts: Ash'aris cite it for divine creation of acts with human acquisition (kasb); Sufis read it as tawhid of action.
